newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka exchange seeks new premises as stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka exchange seeks new premises as stocks rise.

text.p: Bangladesh stocks, the world's hottest over the past two months, could literally fall through the floor, with building authorities warning on Wednesday that the cracked trading area could collapse any time.
The news came as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) asked the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) to lower the daily share price limit to five percent from 10 percent to avert a possible crash.
The DSE index closed 61.06 points higher at 3,648.74 on Tuesday, nearly double its level two months ago, and brokers said on Wednesday they expect further rises over the next few months.
"The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) was built in the early 1960s and may not be able to take the increasing load, (it) may collapse at any time," the Capital City Development Corporation said.
The corporation approves all new buildings and is charged with supervising their safety.
DSE officials said they were looking for a new, bigger premises, but had yet to make a choice.
They added they would decide at a meeting later on Wednesday whether to take the advice of the SEC "to impose a five-precent circuit breaker on traded shares".
However, thousands of punters on streets outside the DSE building appeared unruffled by either developments.
"We don't give a damn what the SEC or DSE says. It's time to cash in on an unexpectedly bouyant market," investor Zamirul Huq said.

"Even authorised brokers, who are supposed to trade only on the DSE floor, are now competing with us in the kerb market," he told Reuters. "Share prices on the street are higher than on the DSE floor."
On Wednesday, many street traders were seen using mobile phones and walkie-talkies, which until recently were confined to the very rich and police.
"Using them (mobile phones and walkie-talkies) has become necessary as trading and income go up," trader Shamsul Alam said.

Police meanwhile sounded a note of caution on the market's bull run. "A large number of criminals, terrorists, thugs and armed activists have apparently given up their usual business and turned to the stock market," a police statement said.
